lawyer:
Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate ----- For the petitioner 
Mr. Md. Khurshedul Alam, DAG with Mr. Delowar Hossain Somadder, AAG & Mr. Monjur Kader, AAG ----- For the opposite-party.
full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, J: On an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 filed by the petitioner, a Rule was issued calling upon the State-opposite-party to show cause as to why the order of conviction and sentence dated 08.02.2011 passed by the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and Executive Magistrate, Jamalganj, Sunamganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 07 of 2011 convicting him under Section 189 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentencing him thereunder to suffer simple imprisonment for 4(four) months and to pay a fine of Tk. 2,000/-, in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a further period of 1(one) month should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 On 07.02.2011, one Ajoy Kumar Das, Surveyor, Upazilla Land Office, Jamalganj, Sunamganj lodged a written complaint with the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and Executive Magistrate, Jamalganj, Sunamganj against the convict-petitioner on the allegations, inter alia, that on that day (07.02.2011) at about 10.00 A. M., the convict-petitioner came to the office of Ajoy Kumar Das and wanted to know about a delimitation matter from him and that Ajoy Kumar Das told him that the delimitation matter would be settled in co-ordination with the Officer-in-Charge, Jamalganj Police Station according to the directive of the office of the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer contained in Memo dated 25.01.2011. On hearing the reply of Ajoy Kumar Das, the petitioner got incensed, took him to task and held out threats of injury to him for immediate resolution of the matter. On receipt of the written complaint, the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and Executive Magistrate, Jamalganj took cognizance of the offence under Section 189 of the Penal Code against the petitioner on 07.02.2011 and directed the Officer-in-Charge of Jamalganj Police Station to get the offence investigated by a Sub-Inspector of Police. The petitioner was tracked down by the police on 07.02.2011 at about 7.50 P. M. and was produced before the Executive Magistrate and the Executive Magistrate by his order no. 2 dated 07.02.2011 sent him to police custody at the Police Station and fixed 08.02.2011 for trial. Anyway, a Sub-Inspector of Police of Jamalganj Police Station investigated the alleged offence and submitted a prosecution report against the petitioner on 08.02.2011. Thereafter the Executive Magistrate framed charge against the petitioner, recorded the plea of guilty and convicted and sentenced him by the impugned order dated 08.02.2011 under Section 189 of the Penal Code as aforesaid. It is the case of the petitioner that the impugned conviction datecl 08.02.2011 by the Executive Magistrate was without jurisdiction and as such, he approached this Court under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 6. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan further submits that the Mobile Court Ain does not contemplate lodging of any complaint by any person and there is no scope for submission of any prosecution report against an accused and there is no provision whatsoever within the four corners of the Ain that empowers the Executive Magistrate to detain him in police custody; but the Executive Magistrate, in flagrant violation of the mandatory provisions of the Ain, received a written complaint from the Surveyor Ajoy Kumar Das, directed the Officer-in-Charge of Jamalganj Police Station to get the alleged offence investigated by a Sub-Inspector of Police and after investigation, the Sub-Inspector of Police submitted a prosecution report against the petitioner and the petitioner was admittedly kept in police custody on the night between 07.02.2011 and 08.02.2011 and the entire proceedings of the case from their very initiation to the passing of the impugned conviction were an abuse of the process of the Court and consequently, the same should be quashed to secure the ends of justice. 

 13. From a combined reading of the provisions of Section 4 and Section 6(l), it is abundantly clear that the authorized Executive Magistrate or the authorized District Magistrate, as the case may be, manning the Mobile Court must take cognizance of the alleged offence instantly at the spot provided the same has been committed or unfolded in his presence and convict the accused and award the prescribed sentence to him on the basis of his plea of guilty under the Ain. But in the present case before us. it is undisputed that the alleged offence was neither committed nor unfolded at the spot in the presence of the Executive Magistrate. So the question of taking cognizance of the alleged offence on 07.02.2011 and convicting the petitioner on 08.02.2011 on the plea of his guilty at the office of the Executive Magistrate is out of the question. 

 18. We are completely at one with the contention of Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan that there is no provision whatsoever within the four corners of the Mobile Court Ain for lodgment of a written complaint with the Executive Magistrate and detaining an accused in police custody at the Police Station prior to his trial. The Ain does not envisage taking cognizance of any scheduled offence and holding trial thereof on different dates as were done in the instant case by the Executive Magistrate. Precisely speaking, the procedural due process was not complied with by the Executive Magistrate causing grave prejudice to the petitioner and rendering his conviction `non-est' in the eye of law. 

 21. The literal construction of the preamble and the provisions of Sections 4, 6(1) and 7(1) and (2) of the Mobile Court Ain does not lead to any absurdity or ambiguity or nebulousness or vagueness. The words used therein are clear and free from any kind of ambiguity or equivocation. According to the plain and literal meaning of the preamble and the provisions of Sections 4, 6(1) and 7(1) and (2) of the Ain, the Executive Magistrate did not take the proceedings against the petitioner. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it transpires that the entire exercise was void and without jurisdiction. The Executive Magistrate did not care to read the relevant provisions of the Ain prior to taking cognizance of the alleged offence and holding the trial of the petitioner on the basis of the prosecution report submitted by a Sub-Inspector of Police of Jamalganj Police Station, Sunamganj. 

 22. As to the contention of the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr. Md. Khurshedul Alam that the Rule is incompetent in view of the fact that the petitioner did not avail himself of the forum of appeal as provided by Section 13 of the Ain, we would like to observe that the entire proceedings of the case right from the beginning to the passing of the impugned order of conviction and sentence were an abuse of the process of the Court and since the same were an abuse of the process of the Court, the petitioner, it seems, rightly invoked the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. This being the scenario, he did not commit any wrong in not exhausting the appellate forum as envisioned by Section 13 of the Ain. 

 23. From the foregoing discussions and regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case, we are led to hold that the impugned conviction of the petitioner was without jurisdiction and null and void. 

 24. Now let us dilate upon the scope of a proceeding under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury and others...Vs...The State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, the Appellate Division clearly spelt out the categories of cases where the High Court Division should interfere under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In that decision, the Appellate Division observed as follows: 

 f) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts, no case can stand against the accused; 

 h) Where there is a legal bar against institution or continuance of a criminal case against an accused person; 

 i) In a case where the allegations in the First Information Report or the Complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged and in such cases, no question of weighing and appreciating evidence arises; and 

 j) The allegations made against the accused person do constitute an offence alleged; but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. 

 25. The above-mentioned categories of cases as spelt out by our Appellate Division in the aforesaid decision reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 were subsequently followed in many decisions including the decision in the case of Ali Akkas...Vs...Enayet Hossain and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44. 

 26. In the case of Sher Ali (Md) and others...Vs...The State reported in 46 DLR(AD) 67, the Appellate Division has held that the inherent power may be invoked independent of powers conferred by any other provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and this power may be exercised to quash a proceeding or even a conviction on conclusion of a trial if the Court concerned had no jurisdiction to hold the said trial or the facts alleged against the accused do not constitute any criminal offence, or the conviction has been based on 'no evidence' or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. 

 27. We have already found that the entire proceedings of the case were an abuse of the process of the Court and the impugned conviction was without jurisdiction and 'de hors' the law. In the result, we find merit in the Rule. The Rule, therefore, succeeds. 

 29. The impugned order of conviction and sentence dated 08.02.2011 passed by the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and Executive Magistrate, Jamalganj, Sunamganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 07 of 2011 is hereby quashed.
